correctness.rationale: The original odd-characteristic table is correct. The repaired RESULT.md explicitly limits the diagonal presentation, not existence of anisotropic extension norms, to odd characteristic: in characteristic two squaring is bijective, and x²+xy+y² over F_2 is an anisotropic norm. It also makes the full stabilizer of the normalized slope explicit. For odd q the nondegenerate bracket forces center kz. Any bracket similitude divided by its value at 1 fixes 1 and acts by ±1 on the orthogonal line; the central shear parameters then yield the additive K ⋊ (K^× ⋊ <σ>) law. Linear slopes reduce to Frobenius orbits, with one nonzero translation class. For semilinear slopes, conjugation by multiplications gives the q+1 slopes in a norm fiber. When the norm is not 1, 1−aσ is invertible and all translations collapse to one orbit. For norm 1 normalize to σ and quotient by (1−σ)K=ker Tr; the slope centralizer comprises k^× and its composites with σ, acting by scalar multiplication on the trace. The two orbits have q and Q−q lifts per slope and give sizes q(q+1) and q(Q−1). The seven rows sum with multiplicities to 2Q(Q−1); counting their classes gives (Q+3q)/2 and the commuting-pair formula by the centralizer sum. Squaring shows that exactly the linear −1 class and the semilinear norm-one, zero-trace class are the nonidentity involutions. These arguments also apply over nonprime k; no step requires the prime-field Frobenius in place of the relative q-Frobenius.
residual_risks: The scope repair does not assert a class distribution for algebras in characteristic two. The finite reproduction corroborates, not replaces, the proof over all odd prime powers.

originality.rationale: The surviving claim is the full uniform seven-row distribution with explicit norm and trace strata, not the known group structure, the basic affine orbit method, or the order-144 example alone. The strongest inspected comparisons establish some ingredients and linear specializations, but do not determine the semilinear class-size strata without an additional orbit calculation. The replacement scope and proof clarification do not enlarge the claimed family or change these comparisons.
residual_risks: A uniform table under affine semilinear, Singer-normalizer, or orthogonal-similitude terminology may exist beyond this bounded comparison. The small-group table was not retrieved, and the scope repair does not establish historical priority.

value.rationale: For this natural full algebra automorphism group, the exact class-size distribution answers more than the known abstract group identification or a total class count: it separates fixed-point-free semilinear slopes from the two classes with the same norm but different translation obstruction. The distinction determines exact centralizer sizes and explains the second involution class uniformly over nonprime as well as prime fields. This provides a useful intrinsic invariant, rather than a single small-group recomputation. The repaired explanation does not pretend to extend that contribution to characteristic two.
residual_risks: The contribution is an inner-conjugacy invariant for this family, not an irreducible character classification or a statement for all binary forms.
